title: the Range header cursor is advanced by a fixed skip past the end of its file-scope chunk and the parse reads on inside the same block
live_proof: absent at the 4.6.8 pin, read two-sided from the pinned tree: the vulnerable unconditional skips have ZERO occurrences in v4.6.8:epan/dissectors/packet-http.c (grep 'first_range_num_str += 6' and 'str += 8' both 0), while the fix's own RFC 9110 range-set commentary is present (3 occurrences of 'ranges-specifier'/'range-unit'), and the pin parses with bounds-aware ws_strtou64(pos, &pos, &first_range_num) at :3936 and :3955 instead of pointer skips. The pre-fix shape is quoted from 0261fd7da6^ at packet-http.c:3740-3745 (the '+= 6' site) and :3788-3790 (the '+= 8' site this case models).
object: the Range header value copied into file scope, 6 bytes for the value used here
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive for the whole case. This is the corpus's only spatial row: no lifetime ends, the cursor simply leaves the chunk. The field is required by the schema and is answered honestly rather than left to imply a reuse that does not happen.
shape: cursor advanced past its chunk by a fixed skip, read inside the same block
allocator_layer: block -- wmem file scope (WMEM_ALLOCATOR_BLOCK). Note that in the corpus harness the bound that fires is wm_narrow()'s per-allocation shrink, not the chunk adapter's.
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. wmem_strdup is written as its own alloc+copy because the corpus seam includes wmem_core only; the skip is upstream's literal 8; the parse that follows is reduced to its first read, which is the byte the cursor lands on.
distinguishing: RETRACTED AND REPLACED 2026-10-05 by the run. The case was filed claiming that sublet completes and sublet-chunks faults, i.e. that it discriminates the chunk port. It does not, and cannot in this harness: src/shared/wmem-port-hooks.h:11-15 narrows EVERY wmem allocation to its request under WM_DOMAIN, so both builds bound the 6-byte object to 6 bytes and both fault with cause 5. Measured on both: WM_CHUNKS=ON and WM_CHUNKS=OFF each fault at the labelled read probe with the pc equal to the resolved probe address. What the case DOES establish is still worth having: it is the corpus's only row that faults on BOUNDS (cause 5) rather than on revoked authority (cause 24), and the first upstream SPATIAL defect reduced anywhere in this tree. The 'a nested allocator hides the extent from malloc' contrast needs an arm with genuinely malloc-granular bounds, which this harness has none of; it lives in the tshark APP port, whose measured fx12 length ladder is level0 41908912, shrink 8388560, sublet 1048528, chunks 64.
note: File scope, not the packet pool, which is why upstream's own defect is here: wmem_file_scope() is a BLOCK allocator. Under THIS harness the scope choice turns out not to change the reading, because wm_narrow() bounds every wmem allocation whatever the scope; it matters for the tshark APP port, where the chunk adapter covers BLOCK and leaves BLOCK_FAST alone. docs/ref/wireshark-spatial-defect-triage.md records the two LIVE spatial defects that sit in BLOCK_FAST for exactly that reason.

spatial.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe
spatial.note: MEASURED, and it REFUTES the prediction this arm first carried ("the sequence completes: bounds are malloc-granular"). This port narrows EVERY wmem allocation to its request -- src/shared/wmem-port-hooks.h:11-15, wm_narrow(), unconditional under WM_DOMAIN -- so no arm of this harness has malloc-granular bounds and a spatial overread faults on all of them.

sublet.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe
sublet.note: MEASURED on the WM_CHUNKS=OFF build, which oracle_arm() judges against this arm. Also refutes its first prediction of completion, and for the same reason as the spatial arm: wm_narrow() is what bounds the object, not the chunk port.

sublet-chunks.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe
sublet-chunks.note: MEASURED on the WM_CHUNKS=ON build. The chunk port narrows the chunk a second time at chunks.c:78, but the bound that the overread crosses is already wm_narrow()'s, so this arm is not the discriminator here -- see 'distinguishing'.

poisoncap-spatial.oracle: PREDICTED and UNMEASURABLE HERE: the sequence completes if mode 0 bounds per malloc, which is what the block arrives as. If PoisonCap narrows each wmem chunk instead, this arm faults and the prediction is wrong -- recorded this way so the reading settles it rather than confirming an assumption.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES, not caught. the platform's own bounds control fired in the same boot: cheribsd-bounds runs abi-probe oob, which sets bounds to exactly 16 and reads offset 16, and it PASSED alongside cheribsd-abi reporting CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1. A spatial completion is therefore a reading, not a silent detector. NOTE, corrected in the same edit: this arm previously said CHERI bounds the g_malloc'd block. On this harness there is no per-block malloc -- shared/driver.c hands the allocator ONE 384 MiB arena and src/native/regions.c carves it by bumping a cursor -- so the only CHERI bound in play is the arena. The completion is real; the reason is weaker than the arm used to claim.
cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap built on this host with tests/cheri-baseline/provision-cheri-vehicle.sh (kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, releng/26.07-88f39900c329 = pins.env's CHERIBSD_REV; hw.machine_arch riscv64c; qemu 16135483052dfdd6, firmware f0e1fe57b0f85075, kernel 8ab453f46dc76cf2, libc fdce2289224bb519, image 0cb16209c16c5edf) -- the same vehicle, hash for hash, as the memcached allocator-repros run of the same day, so the readings are directly comparable.

native-detect.oracle: NO ASan report, and that is the finding rather than a gap: the overread stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks for ASan to poison. Needs its own positive control -- a read past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- or a silent arm proves nothing about the subject and something about the instrument.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.

status: MEASURED 2026-10-05 under QEMU, both builds, case 13 only, modes spatial and sublet. WM_CHUNKS=ON: both arms fault, cause 5, at the labelled read probe, pc 0x10190222c equal to the resolved probe address. WM_CHUNKS=OFF: both arms fault, cause 5, pc 0x1019013f8 likewise. N=1 per cell. The run REFUTED the completion predictions both arms were filed with; the oracles above are the corrected, measured ones and 'distinguishing' records the withdrawal. poisoncap-* and cheribsd-revocation remain predictions -- neither platform is on this host. native-detect remains not written and still needs its own positive control before a silent ASan arm means anything. CheriBSD MEASURED 2026-10-06 on a vehicle built on this host, revocation on: completes, not caught.
